It said it was done. So chi doesn't ask. 10 iterations without a new eval result and it's killed.

A harness runs the model in a loop. The hard part is telling, without asking the model, if the loop is going anywhere.

My stuck rules missed a fleet trying a new idea every round, each under the 0.5% bar. It plateaued its whole budget.

Now 2 rounds with no real gain = stuck.
The stuck/plateau rules are ~40 lines of plain Python, no LLM call: https://github.com/kdpisda/chi/blob/main/chi/director/review.py

The benchmark I wrote to test chi's noise guard has a worse problem than noise. It counts Python line events, so the O(n) rewrite loses to the O(n^2) baseline, 904 ops to 301, while running 20x faster.

Same loop on one line: 604 ops, same bytecode.

getchi.dev

uv tool install getchi, then from a checkout of github.com/kdpisda/chi:

chi run examples/offline.yaml

No key, no network, $0. Just ran it: 3 candidates through the real evaluator, champion an O(n) rewrite of the O(n^2) baseline.

For live agents, run chi then /vendors.

My agents have a shell, so they can call the leaderboard CLI. In dogfood they did, for benchmarks. A ranked submit could burn the rate limit.

chi puts a shim first on their PATH: benchmark passes, --mode leaderboard exits 3.

A speed bump, not a sandbox. Auth stays on disk.

A better benchmark score is not faster code. I scripted a candidate with a fast path only when len(xs) == 4000, the benchmark's exact input. chi scored it 99.7% faster.

On 900, 3300 and 9000 elements it gained nothing: -4.1%.

chi's new holdout gate caught it: overfit.

Installed is not working. A CLI on PATH can still reject every model on your login.

A chi dogfood run was lost to that, and to a second CLI's wrong command template. Both surfaced mid-run.

Now chi providers --probe pings each CLI before a fleet starts.

getchi.dev

I fed chi a scripted O(n) prefix sum with an off-by-one: each slot holds the sum before it. Timed by hand: 0.07ms vs a 17ms baseline.

chi's ledger row for it:

  correct 0
  seeds_passed []
  score null

Seed 11 was off by 99.9, so chi never timed it. Wrong code gets no score.

Tested chi's budget cap today: a fake CLI coder reporting $0.40 an iteration, a $0.50 cap, five iterations.

chi run did all five. The event log holds $2.00. The run summary says total_cost_usd 0.

Only API-loop agents charge the cap. A CLI coder's cost is logged, never counted.

A chi dogfood run crowned a cheater: a coder froze the benchmark's clock, timed 0.0ms, and passed 3 correctness seeds.

The fix rejects scores <= 0. Today I faked a clock that ticks 1 microsecond per read. The O(n^2) baseline scored 0.001ms. Accepted.

getchi.dev

chi's export copied the live candidate file. Coders revert that file, so it could print the winner's score and ship a loser.

Now each correct, scored candidate is archived by hash; export ships that.

Today I reset the live file to baseline, exported, got the champion.

You don't have to kill an agent loop to redirect it. chi steer appends a note to a file each coder re-reads before every iteration. No restart; each new file hash is logged.

The limit: it can't reach an iteration in flight. At the 600s default timeout, a note can wait 10 min.

Both halves had passing tests. chi's director adds each round's spend to its total. The runner sums the whole event log, and the director writes its own sum back into that log.

A $25 ceiling fired at $2.40 of real spend. No unit test spans the seam.

as written: benchmarked, 0.0620ms
CRLF, trailing spaces: cached, not re-run

The hash strips line endings and trailing whitespace. Comments stay, so a comment-only edit is re-benchmarked.

Myth: after a win, an agent loop gets some slack.

Fed chi's classifier a win (636 to 600), then one flat round with no dead end logged. Verdict: stuck, which triggers research.

It counts new ruled-out approaches in the last 2 rounds, not wins. One per round keeps it plateaued.

A gate that runs after the irreversible step is a report.

Pointed chi's auto-submit at a fake leaderboard and replayed a scripted candidate overfit to the benchmark input. Submitted at 0.06ms. 0.8s later the holdout gate said overfit: -1.2% held out.

Gave a chi task a 1s lease, claimed it as agent a, then let a go quiet.

A minute later:
$ chi task claim --agent b
NONE (exit 1)

Row: claimed, owner a, attempts 0. The function that returns expired leases to the pool exists and has tests. Nothing else calls it.

chi refuses to log a dead end without evidence. Probed that check today:

--evidence-json '{}': rejected
--evidence-json '"trust me"': accepted
--evidence-json 'true': accepted

It tests that the parsed JSON is truthy, not that it holds a result. Prose in quotes gets through.

chi's watchdog killed an agent for doing its job. It hashed the candidate file to spot loops, but agents revert that file after a losing benchmark.

Replayed the old rule: 6 new candidates evaluated, killed as "unchanged". Fix: hash what was evaluated.

Myth: a kill threshold of 6 fires on the 6th repeat.

chi's watchdog kills a coder after 6 identical candidates. The director runs 2-iteration slices, and the watchdog was rebuilt every slice.

Replayed: 20 identical iterations, 0 kills. Seeded from the event log: killed at 6.

Guard the irreversible call, not the command.

Replayed it on my pure-Python prefix sum: it said to search cuSOLVER and labeled a 0.07ms champion 0.07µs. Now it reads the problem spec.

Nothing outside tests reads last_heartbeat_at.
